Cambridge, MA & San Diego, CA

Business has always felt personal to me. It started with watching my mom build something from nothing.

I'm Mila, a sophomore at Harvard studying Economics, with a secondary in Mind, Brain & Behavior. This is the story of how growing up around my mom starting GoMacro got me interested in the business world, and where that's taken me since.

LinkedIn
Where it started

The GoMacro story

I grew up in San Diego watching my mom start a nutrition bar company called GoMacro. It was inspiring in a way I didn't have words for yet, she built it with no funding and no business background, and I got to watch it happen from the inside.

In middle school, I started working with the marketing team: helping out at photoshoots, drafting outreach to influencers, learning what it actually takes to get a brand in front of people. As I got older, I started sitting in on meetings across departments (sales, ops, finance) and I noticed I kept gravitating toward the same room every time. Finance.

A pattern I noticed about myself

When I see room to build something, I build it

Almost every project I've taken on started the same way: I noticed something was missing, and instead of waiting for someone else to fix it, I built it myself.

Middle school

My first Etsy shop

Inspired by watching my mom build a brand from scratch, I started my own small shop, my first real attempt at running something end to end.

2022 to present

Helped start my church's disability ministry

I helped launch KidVenture's KV Buddies program, which pairs volunteers one-to-one with kids with disabilities so they can participate in mainstream programs alongside their peers.

2023 to 2025

Founded my high school's first business class and DECA chapter

I pitched the head of school on a business class and a DECA chapter, then built both from scratch, including student-run shops, a coffee shop and an apparel line. DECA grew into the school's largest student organization within a year.

2024

Led my school's first trip to Harvard's BOLD Conference

As part of bringing more business opportunities to my high school, I served as an ambassador for Harvard's Women in Business BOLD Conference, recruited attendees, fundraised so more students could go, and led the first group from my school to attend.

2023 to present

Founded the Friendship Trios Program at Autism Tree

Inspired by my aunt, who's on the spectrum, I designed a program that pairs one volunteer with two kids on the spectrum who share similar interests, after noticing how much parents worried about their kids' ability to make friends.

The other half of my personality

I like to compete, and I like to win

I grew up in individual sports (dance, gymnastics, tennis, triple jump) where there's nowhere to hide and no one else to credit or blame. I captained both my high school tennis and track teams.

That same instinct followed me into business. I don't just want to participate in something, I want to be the best at it. On the Harvard Crimson's Business Board, that's meant closing more advertising revenue than anyone else on the team.

What I'm learning right now

Staying curious

In high school, I published research on the connection between neuroscience and marketing, and separately on autism: its causes, current diagnostics, and behavioral interventions, work that grew out of my passion for autism, inspired by my aunt, who's on the spectrum. One of those pieces was recognized among the year's best articles out of hundreds published.

What I'm most curious about right now is deals: reading the news on live M&A, watching founders, some of whom I've admired for years, decide to sell what they built, and trying to understand the thinking behind that decision. That curiosity is what's pushed me to actually learn the mechanics behind it: LBOs, DCF analysis, M&A structuring, the vocabulary of investment banking and private equity.

What shaped me outside the classroom

Seeing the world

Some of the experiences that have shaped me most happened far from a classroom or an office. I've gone on mission trips to the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica, building homes and playgrounds and spending time with kids in communities very different from my own. During a summer consulting internship in Cape Town, I spent my mornings before work watching the sunrise from the mountains above the city.

Where this is all headed

Why investment banking

For a long time, I knew I wanted to be in business because of my mom, but I didn't know where to start. That changed when I started talking with my older brother, who's headed into investment banking himself, and started following live M&A deals, watching founders of companies I admired make one of the biggest decisions of their lives.

What excites me most about this industry is getting to sit on that side of the table: working on live, high-stakes transactions, and helping founders like my mom navigate the decision to sell what they built. That's what brought me here.
